meaning: From Triakis: Greek tri- “three” + akís “point”, for teeth with one large central cusp flanked on each side by a small cusplet; -idae “family of”
description: Small to medium, slender sharks with two large spineless dorsal fins and oval eyes. They feed on the seabed and in open water in warm and temperate seas, and include the smooth-hounds and the tope.
